claim_reviews.conclusion: “Secondhand item” correctly expresses an item previously owned or used.
claim_reviews.subject: English cue and sense

claim_reviews.conclusion: Correct, natural Indonesian wording for a used or secondhand item.
claim_reviews.subject: Indonesian answer: barang bekas

claim_reviews.conclusion: Valid Malaysian Malay wording for secondhand goods/items; “barang terpakai” is also used, so the proposed form is a preference rather than an exclusive equivalent.
claim_reviews.subject: Malaysian answer: barangan terpakai

claim_reviews.conclusion: Acceptable as a regional lexical-preference label, provided it does not imply that either form is unavailable in the other variety.
claim_reviews.subject: Final relation: different-common-word

claim_reviews.conclusion: No false-friend contrast is supplied or needed; “bekas” and “terpakai” both relate to prior use in these phrases.
claim_reviews.subject: False-friend contrast

response.rationale: Both forms are valid and match the cue “secondhand item” / “item previously owned or used.” “Barang bekas” is established Indonesian usage; Malaysian sources support “barangan terpakai” and the closely related “barang terpakai.” The contrast is useful as a regional preference, though not exclusive, and no false-friend issue is present.
